frameworks.justification: Reflects the complementary relationship between pedagogical strategies and cognitive development, while explicitly addressing trade-offs with challenges. Grounded in high-robustness relationships (n=10-15 studies) between skill development and implementation frameworks.
frameworks.general_objective: To investigate how GenAI-mediated pedagogical strategies facilitate cognitive skill development while navigating implementation challenges

specific_objectives.text: Examine structured implementation models' role in fostering analytical reasoning
Evaluate cognitive regulation patterns during human-AI co-creative processes
Document contradictions between domain-specific competency gains and over-reliance consequences

limitations: Limited coverage of humanistic competency aspects

frameworks.justification: Aligns with the identified analytical axes 'Efficacy vs. Integration Trade-offs' and 'Skill Development Approaches'. Captures 60-70% of studies through contrasting cognitive development paradigms.
frameworks.general_objective: To compare analytical reasoning enhancement versus domain-specific competency outcomes across GenAI implementation models

specific_objectives.text: Analyze critical thinking development in language/clinical simulations
Evaluate structured models (GASA, GenAI-PP) against co-creative frameworks
Investigate ambiguity management in ethical-integration contexts

strengths: Clear methodological distinction between implementation approaches

frameworks.justification: Mirrors the emergent taxonomy's hierarchical structure and documented implementation patterns. Built on high-robustness pedagogical strategy research (10-15 studies).
frameworks.general_objective: To map sequential development from pedagogical design to cognitive outcomes and challenge mitigation

specific_objectives.text: Identify implementation models enabling scenario-based learning
Assess resulting analytical reasoning and domain competency gains
Develop adaptive frameworks for managing cognitive dependencies

strengths: Natural progression from design to mitigation
limitations: Linear assumption may overlook complex interactions

data.recommendation: Framework 1 (Integration and Outcomes) is recommended as it captures the most robust relationships (n=10-15 studies for key connections), balances efficacy with critical limitations, and directly addresses all three analytical axes. Its estimated 60-70% coverage ensures comprehensive engagement with the literature while acknowledging the medium robustness of challenge-related findings (n=8-10).
